title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-07-15
content:
Week: 2026-07-08 -> 2026-07-15
Owner: Lina Park (serving-runtime)
Summary:
- Focus this week: finalize fused attention kernel rollout for 8-bit quantized paths, KV cache eviction tuning for long-tail sessions, and stabilize dynamic batching heuristics for bursty traffic.
- Short wins: small p50 token latency gains on small-medium models; longer work remains on edge-case tail latencies.

Kernel work
- Merged PR #1842: fused attention path for q4_0 and q8_0. Microbenchmarks on A100 (4x16GB) show: p50 per-token latency improvement ~12% for 2048-context on seq-len=512, p95 improved ~6%.
- Notes: nvfuser-backed fallback still ~8% slower for short sequences; we keep fallback for GPUs where kernel fails.
- Action: Marco to run full regression across model zoo (due 2026-07-22).
- Blocker: intermittent launch failures on older driver stacks (CUDA 12.*). Devon and infra are reproducing (JIRA-RT-7623).

KV cache
- Experimented with LRU eviction + TTL hybrid for interactive sessions. Observed cache hit-rate increase from 68% -> 78% for multi-turn chat workload (avg session length 14 turns).
- Memory: compressed shard serialization (lz4) reduces host memory pressure ~30% but adds ~1.8ms to cold-start token for first lookup. Tradeoff acceptable for Dedicated customers.
- Action: A/B rollout to 20% traffic next week; owner: Aisha Khan.

Batching and scheduling
- Dynamic batcher heuristics updated to prioritize latency-SLO routes (route metadata). Under synthetic burst tests (10k rps -> spike), tail latency p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 1.1s while throughput preserved.
- Discovered a pathological case: many tiny requests to long-context models caused queue inversion, increasing median latency by ~15%. Proposed short-term mitigation: cap per-worker inflight tokens and route tiny-requests to a fast-path.
- Action: Priya to prototype fast-path routing (RFC by 2026-07-20).

Metrics snapshot (internal runner env):
- Model: redwood-7b-compat, seq=512, batcher=config-v3
- p50 token latency: 8.6ms (baseline 9.8ms pre-kernel)
- p95 token latency: 28ms (baseline 30ms)
- KV cache hit rate: 78% (after hybrid eviction)
- GPU utilization (avg): 62%
- Tokens/sec per GPU: 112k

Incidents / Bugs
- CUDA driver regression causing kernel launch error on older infra images. Impact: 2 Dedicated clusters with pinned images. Mitigation: pin to safe driver and schedule rolling upgrade. Owner: Devon.

Meetings / Syncs
- Paired review with infra on kernel rollout checklist (07/13) — agreed to add canary validation for memory spikes.
- Cross-team sync with product-hosted-api to discuss latency SLOs and default batching configs (07/14).

Decisions
- Rollout fused attention kernels to hosted API canary (10% traffic) on Monday 2026-07-20 assuming no regressions on full model zoo tests.
- Adopt LRU+TTL hybrid for interactive sessions in Dedicated by default; opt-out flag for sensitive workloads.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How aggressive should compression be for KV shards in Private deployments where disk I/O profiles vary? (Investigate I/O-bound customers).
- Should we expose a per-route batching hint in the public API? Product requested prototype.

Action items
- Marco Rossi: full model zoo regression + perf dashboard (due 2026-07-22).
- Aisha Khan: start 20% A/B rollout of hybrid KV eviction (due 2026-07-21).
- Devon Chen: root cause for CUDA regression and coord with infra for image pinning (in progress).
- Priya Nair: prototype fast-path routing for tiny requests (RFC 2026-07-20).
- Lina Park: prepare canary checklist and rollback plan for kernel rollout (due 2026-07-19).

Notes to self / informal
- Keep eyes on the p99 during canary — small percentage of sessions still show elevated tail latencies. Likely related to garbage-collection spikes in python wrappers.
- Consider adding a lightweight C++ tracer around kernel launches to capture timing without python overhead.

Attachments / refs:
- perf dashboard link (internal): dashboards/serving-runtime/kernel-kv-batching-2026-07
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1842
- Jira: JIRA-RT-7623

End of note.
